A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-PGC research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, captioning, grounding, and entailment attack results, together with ablations, defense evaluations, and cross-domain experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original attack experiments and additionally reports alternative-loss comparisons and semantic-similarity measurements in Tables 9 and 10.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the conditional generator, cross-attention, farthest-positive selection, contrastive and unimodal losses, and word-substitution procedure. Expanded descriptions and changed notation do not establish an altered method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate retrieval on Flickr30K/MSCOCO, captioning on MSCOCO, grounding on RefCOCO+, and entailment on SNLI-VE. Cross-dataset and defended scenarios remain. The added loss and semantic-similarity analyses do not establish new dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds ETU to R@1 retrieval and alignment-distance comparisons, and replaces GAP with ETU in the R@5/R@10 comparison (v2 Table 8; v3 Table 7). Figure 2 adds UAP_PGD, while Table 10 newly compares Co-Attack and SGA on semantic similarity.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs compare cosine, MSE, and contrastive objectives with and without the unimodal loss, and measure BERTScore precision, recall, and F1 over 5,000 sentence pairs. Existing splits, attack budgets, augmentation, training sample counts, and training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of contrastive loss against alternative distance objectives and a quantitative analysis of text semantic preservation (Appendices D–E). It removes the image-only ablation isolating textual perturbation's contribution (v2 Table 9) and one retrieval example. Existing defense, sensitivity, and cross-domain analyses remain despite relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the attack results. Dataset/model averages and Gaussian augmentation noise do not constitute changed uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds baseline, alternative-loss, and BERTScore results and removes image-only ablation scores. CLIP_CNN-source retrieval and cross-domain rows change; for example, Flickr30K white-box R@1 TR/IR changes from 81.74/88.90 to 96.50/94.22 under unchanged stated settings (Table 1). MSCOCO GAP rows also change, with v3 Table 5 repeating the Flickr30K values for CLIP_CNN and BLIP sources. Most other retained results match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same attack constraints, attention operation, losses, optimization objective, and relative-distance definition. Equation 3 merely abbreviates exponentiated similarity. The new loss rationale is conceptual; no substantive mathematical derivation or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: universal multimodal attacks using cross-modal conditioning and malicious contrastive training, with effectiveness across models and tasks. The added comparisons support and contextualize these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix F explicitly describes conspicuous semantic failures, gives an ungrammatical substitution example, and restricts an embedding-based remedy to white-box access. v3 Appendices E/G instead infer a favorable efficacy–stealthiness balance from BERTScore, attribute competitors' semantic drift to their word-selection mechanisms, and replace those concrete caveats with milder improvement suggestions.

D1.justification: v3 removes the GitHub repository pointer and the dedicated dataset descriptions. It explicitly clarifies that retrieval ASR is calculated over originally correct predictions and identifies the generator as decoder-based. Existing training details remain; removal of the link does not establish that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused positioning against concurrent ETU, emphasizing its image-only, nongenerative approach. It also adds references including DeepFool, BERTScore, and textual UAP research, while removing Hashemi et al. (2020). The broader related-work organization and research framing remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and numerous introduction, method, and evaluation paragraphs are rewritten. The narrative moves defenses into the appendix, reverses the captioning/grounding presentation order, removes the dataset-introduction section, reorganizes the appendices, and recasts limitations as discussions. Author and affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, redraws introductory illustrations, and rearranges the comparison plots. The original combined retrieval table is split between main text and appendix and expanded with ETU. New analysis tables appear, the image-only table disappears, and retrieval visualizations move to the appendix with one example removed.

improvement.justification: The added concurrent baselines and loss/semantic analyses address validation gaps in v2. However, v3 introduces unexplained reporting inconsistencies: Table 5 repeats Flickr30K GAP rows under MSCOCO, and its contrastive-loss-only ALBEF TR result is 76.46 in Table 9 versus 79.54 in the retained Table 4 ablation. Removing the image-only ablation and weakening concrete semantic-failure caveats also reduces transparency. These benefits and reliability losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
